issues.description: PersonResource constructor parameter and initialization mismatch: In the solution repository, the class de.tum.in.ase.eist.rest.PersonResource declares a constructor public PersonResource(de.tum.in.ase.eist.service.NoteService noteService) that sets this.personService = null. The template and the problem statement expect PersonResource to receive a PersonService and assign it to the personService field (i.e., public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; }). The current solution constructor accepts the wrong service type and leaves personService null, causing compilation/type mismatch and runtime NPEs and confusing students implementing the endpoints.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in the solution repository to accept a PersonService and assign it to the personService field. Example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; } Ensure the constructor parameter type matches the field type so personService is properly initialized and endpoints can call personService without NPEs.

issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for the PersonResource dependency: The problem statement and template expect PersonResource to depend on and receive a PersonService (the Person-related business layer). In the template (src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java) the PersonResource declares a field 'private final PersonService personService' and its constructor accepts a PersonService parameter (PersonService personService) and assigns it to this.personService. In the solution (src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java) the constructor signature incorrectly accepts a NoteService parameter (de.tum.in.ase.eist.service.NoteService noteService) and assigns this.personService = null. Students reading the artifacts will be unable to map the Person endpoints to the intended PersonService implementation, and dependency injection semantics are broken in the solution, which will confuse or block them when understanding or running the server.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution's PersonResource constructor to accept a PersonService parameter and assign it to the personService field. For example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; } Ensure imports/types reference de.tum.in.ase.eist.service.PersonService so the injected service matches the template and the problem description.
